_comment: Things met on the road that are not (at first) a fight. where: road (true = only on roads, false = only off them, missing = either), biomes (or ["any"]), danger [min, max], time any/day/night, season list or any. Each option has a label and one of: outcome, check (skill, dc, success, failure) or shop (stock [item, qty], markup). Outcomes: text (one is chosen; {name} is the leader), items [[item, qty or dice]] (negative qty = given away), money (copper; negative = paid), xp, deed, news (true: hear of a place you don't know), fatigue (change), effect [name, hours], loot [[item, dice, chance]], fight (an encounter group), ambush [group, chance], time (minutes). requires: items [[item, qty]] and/or money.

flooded_ford.name: a flooded ford
intro: The ford is under brown water, moving fast, carrying branches. The marker stones are gone.
Rain upriver: the crossing is a torrent, and the far bank is further away than it was.
The river has taken the ford and a good deal of the bank with it. You can hear stones moving in the current.

text: You cross with the water at your chest and your heart in your mouth, and come out shaking.
The current takes your legs. You come out a hundred paces down, soaked, bruised and lighter than you were.
Roped together, each braced against the next, you cross a step at a time and come out on the far side all together.
Halfway over somebody goes under, and the rope brings them up again, coughing. Wet through, but nobody is lost, and nothing much is.
Three hours of wet ground and thorns, and then a fallen tree wide enough to cross on.
You make a fire on the bank and watch the water go down, which it does, slowly, the way water does.

burnt_farm.name: a burnt farm
intro: Black beams, a fallen roof, and a yard where nothing moves. It happened weeks ago, and nobody came back.
A farmstead burned to the sill stones. A dog's chain lies in the ash, with no dog on it.
A burnt steading, the thatch gone, the walls standing. Somebody's boots are still by the door.

text: In a pit under the hearthstone: what they hid and never came back for.
Ash, nails, and a child's shoe. You leave it where it is.

options.label: Dig under the hearth with your shovel

text: The hearthstone comes up, and under it a pit lined with clay: what they hid and never came back for.

options.label: Bury what is left of them

text: It takes an hour, and there is no priest, but it is done, and done properly.
outcome.deed: buried the dead at a burnt farm

text: You keep the ruin on your left and do not look at it twice.

toll_men.name: toll men on the road
intro: A rope across the road, two men with spears, and a third with a ledger. "Bridge toll. Lord's orders."
A toll post: a pole, a hut, and men who look as though the arrangement is recent, and theirs.
A chain across the road, a brazier, and three men who ask for the toll before they say good day.

text: The rope comes down. The man with the ledger writes nothing in it.
"...Right. Go on, then. Quickly, before the sergeant looks up."
"Everyone is exempt, to hear them tell it." You pay, and they take a little extra for the trouble.
Shouting behind you, and a spear that lands nowhere near. Whoever they answer to will hear a description of you.
outcome.deed: refused a toll on the road

broken_cart.name: a carter in trouble
intro: A cart is down to its axle in the ruts, one wheel off, and a carter is arguing with an ox about it.
A wagon leans in the mud with its load shifted. The driver is old, and the light is going.
A carter is heaving at a cart with a split shaft, alone, and getting nowhere.

text: Between you the cart comes up and the wheel goes on. They press what they can spare on you, which is little, and mean it.
success.deed: helped a carter out of the mud

text: An hour of heaving and swearing, and the cart is where it was. They thank you anyway.

options.label: Lever it up with your crowbar

text: A stone for a fulcrum, the crowbar under the axle, and the cart comes up as if it wanted to. The wheel goes on in no time. They press what they can spare on you, which is little, and mean it.
outcome.deed: helped a carter out of the mud

options.label: Take what is on the cart

text: The old carter backs away and lets you. They will describe you to the first guard they meet.
outcome.deed: robbed a carter on the road

text: The mud is deep at the edge, but it is not your cart.

stone_circle.name: a ring of standing stones
intro: Nine stones, or eight and the stump of one, in a ring on the open ground. Older than anything with a name.
Standing stones, lichened and leaning. Sheep have worn a path around the outside, and nothing grows inside.
A ring of stones on the skyline, and a track that goes round it rather than through.

text: You sleep badly, and dream of people walking in a circle, and wake with the feeling of having been counted.
The marks are not decoration. You cannot read them, but you understand that they were a warning, and that it was not meant for you.
Weather-worn scratches, a beetle, and your own patience running out.
Some things are best walked past.

charcoal_burners.name: charcoal burners
intro: Smoke from a covered mound, and two soot-black figures who watch you come with the patience of people who cannot leave their fire.
A charcoal camp in a clearing: the mound smoking, a lean-to, and a dog that does not bark.
A hut of turf and a smoking mound, and a man who watches you the whole way past without a word.

options.label: Share their fire and their talk

text: They talk about the forest the way other people talk about a difficult relative. You warm through, and hear what has been on the roads.
Black bread, black hands, and fuel that will light in any weather.
They watch you out of the clearing and go back to the mound.

sick_child.name: a sick child at a cottage
intro: A woman comes out of a turf cottage at the sound of you and asks, without preamble, whether you have anything for a fever.
A cottage, a thin dog, and a man holding a child who is too quiet. "Is one of you a healer?"
A cottage with the shutters closed in daylight, and somebody inside coughing badly.

text: You show them how to steep it. The child drinks, and sleeps, and the fever will break or it will not — but they have something now.
outcome.deed: gave medicine to a sick child

text: Cool water, a clean cloth and an hour of patience. By the end of it the child is asking for bread.
success.deed: brought a child through a fever

text: You do what can be done, which is not much, and leave them with instructions they will follow and hope they work.

options.label: Give them money for a healer

text: A silver piece is a week's work here. They will walk to the town tonight.
outcome.deed: paid for a healer for a stranger's child

text: It is true, and they know it is true, and it does not help either of you.

drowned_man.name: a body in the reeds
intro: Face down in the reeds, a week in the water, with the crows already disappointed.
A body in the shallows, caught on a root, turning slowly with the current.
Something pale turns over in the eddy under the bank, and turns over again.

text: A purse, swollen leather, and a letter too wet to read. Whoever he was, he is not using them.

options.label: Pull him out and cover him

text: He is heavier than he looks, and you are wet to the waist, and there are stones enough to keep the crows off.
outcome.deed: gave a drowned stranger a grave

text: The river had him first.

caravan.name: a merchant caravan
intro: Six carts, twenty oxen and a dozen hired swords, going the other way at the pace of the slowest wheel.
A caravan is halted at the roadside, resting the beasts. The guards watch you the way guards do; the factor does not look up from his tally.
A line of carts on the road ahead, moving at the pace of the slowest ox, with outriders watching the treeline.

options.label: Walk with them for a while

text: You match their pace for a few hours. Nothing troubles a column this size, and the factor is glad of another sword; at the parting he gives you what he can spare.

options.label: [Intimidation] Ask for a toll of your own

text: The factor looks at the guards, and the guards look at the road, and a purse changes hands. Nobody says the word robbery.
success.deed: shook down a caravan on the road

text: "Move along." Twelve hired swords do not need to say anything else.
The guards form up before you have finished speaking.
outcome.deed: attacked a caravan on the road

text: You step off the road and let the carts go by, and the dust settles slowly.

pedlar.name: a travelling pedlar
intro: A pedlar comes the other way, bent under a pack twice his width, a cudgel through his belt. He raises a hand: friendly, careful.
A woman leading a laden mule has stopped by the road to rest it. She looks you over and decides you might be customers.
A pedlar sits on his pack at the roadside, rubbing his feet, and brightens when he sees company.

options.label: See what there is to buy

text: The talk is of prices, tolls and weather, and then, lower: of a place you did not know about.
You nod and walk on.

pilgrims.name: pilgrims
intro: A file of pilgrims in grey wool trudges along the verge, singing badly. Their leader carries a staff hung with little bells.
Five pilgrims sit by a milestone, sharing a loaf. One waves you over.
Pilgrims, twenty of them, walking two abreast and praying out of step.

text: They share bread and gossip, and ask nothing of you. It is the easiest mile in weeks.
The leader blesses you in a language you do not know. It sounds sincere.
You leave them to their singing.

patrol.name: a patrol
intro: Four spearmen and a sergeant on a tired horse block the road. "Where from, and where to?"
A patrol in the lord's colours waves you to the side of the road. They look bored and underpaid.
Horsemen come up the road at a trot and slow when they see you.

text: The sergeant grunts, waves you on, and as you pass mentions trouble further on.
They do not like your answers. They go through your pack and keep a "road toll" for their trouble.

options.label: Ask them about the dangers hereabouts

text: "Stay on the road," says the sergeant, and tells you why.
Coin changes hands. Suddenly everyone is friends, and the sergeant has a great deal to say about the country ahead.

refugees.name: refugees
intro: A cart with a broken wheel, and around it a family: two children, a grandmother, a man with his arm in a sling. Everything they own is on the cart.
People on the road with bundles and handcarts, faces grey with tiredness, all going the same way: away.
A column of people on foot, carrying what they could, nobody talking.

text: The children eat as if they had forgotten how. The grandmother holds your hand and will not let go for a while.
The man takes it without a word, then turns away so you won't see his face.
Raiders, soldiers, it hardly matters which: the village is ash. They tell you where, and whom to avoid.
You walk on. They do not call after you.

wounded_traveller.name: a wounded traveller
intro: A man sits against a tree, grey-faced, his hands pressed to his side. There is a lot of blood on the grass.
A woman lies by the roadside, one leg twisted under her. She has been there a while.
Somebody is calling out from the ditch, and has been for a while by the sound of it.

text: You stop the bleeding and get water into them. Later, they press a few coins on you and will not take them back.
You do what you can. It is not enough. They die holding your sleeve.
failure.deed: tried to save a dying stranger

text: They watch you do it. Neither of you says anything.
You walk on. The sound follows you further than it should.

abandoned_camp.name: an abandoned camp
intro: A cold fire-pit, a torn lean-to, scattered belongings. Whoever camped here left in a hurry, or didn't leave at all.
Somebody's camp, a few days old: tracks everywhere, a smashed pot, a bedroll kicked into the bushes.
A camp nobody broke properly: the fire kicked over, a boot left behind, the tracks going one way fast.

text: Under the lean-to and in the bushes you find what the owners never came back for.
You turn over the mess for half an hour and find nothing worth carrying.
Whatever happened here, you don't need it to happen to you.

hunters.name: hunters
intro: Two hunters with a deer slung on a pole between them stop to look you over.
A trapper with a string of pelts over one shoulder falls into step beside you.
A hunter steps out of the wood with a bow strung and a hare at his belt, and looks you over.

text: They tell you, more or less. Hunters never tell you everything.
They watch you go, then carry on.

carcass.name: a fresh carcass
intro: A deer lies dead in the grass, throat torn, barely touched. Whatever killed it will be back.
The carcass of an elk, killed within the hour. Crows are gathering but nothing else has come yet.
Flies, a smell, and a sheep opened up ten yards off the road.

text: You work fast and cut away good meat.
You make a mess of it and save little.
You leave it to whatever killed it.

shrine.name: a wayside shrine
intro: A little stone shrine stands at the crossroads, its saint worn faceless by weather. Someone has left fresh flowers and a few coins.
A wooden shrine on a post, roofed with bark. Inside: a carved figure, candle stubs, and offerings.
A cairn with a cross wedged into the top of it, and pennies pushed between the stones.

text: For a few minutes the world is quiet. You feel steadier when you stand.
You add your coin to the others.
outcome.deed: left an offering at a shrine

text: A handful of copper and a cheap brass ring. Nobody saw. Probably.

herbs.name: a patch of herbs
intro: In a sheltered hollow, a patch of plants you half recognise: yarrow, comfrey, perhaps woundwort.
A bank of plants in the shelter of a wall: yarrow, and something that might be comfrey.
Somebody's old physic garden gone wild at the edge of a ruin, and still useful.

text: You pick the right ones and bundle them carefully.
You are not sure which are which, and leave them rather than guess.
You walk on.

hungry_deserters.name: hungry deserters
intro: Three men in stained soldiers' coats step out of the trees. They have weapons but they look more hungry than dangerous. "Food," one says. "Please."
Men in soldiers' rags sit by the road and get up when they see you, slowly, without enthusiasm.
Four of them, thin, with spears they are holding like walking sticks.

text: They eat standing up, like dogs. Then they nod, and go back into the trees.
They look at you, and at each other, and decide you are not worth it.
"Wrong answer," says the one in front, and they draw.
You draw. So do they.

gibbet.name: a gibbet
intro: A gibbet at the crossroads, and in it what is left of a man. A board nailed below says what he did.
Two bodies hang from the old oak by the road, turning slowly. The crows have been at them.
A gibbet, empty, with the cage hanging open and the chain oiled.

text: Banditry on the king's road, it says, and names where. The lord wants the rest of them found.

options.label: Cut them down and bury them

text: It takes an hour. Nobody thanks you, and somebody may mind.
outcome.deed: buried the hanged at a crossroads

text: You walk on, not looking up.

fallen_climber.name: someone fallen into a ravine
intro: A voice from below the path: on a ledge thirty feet down a gully, a goatherd with a twisted leg is shouting up at the sky.
Down in a ravine, on a shelf of rock above the drop, a woman is waving both arms. Her basket of herbs is spread across the stones below her.
Somebody has come off the path: you can see the slide in the scree, and at the bottom of it, on a ledge, a man who cannot climb back.

options.label: Lower a rope and haul them up

text: It takes all of you on the rope, but up they come, white-faced and grateful. They press a few coins on you and limp home.
outcome.deed: pulled a stranger out of a ravine

text: Hand over hand down the crack and back up with them on your back. You will feel it tomorrow.
success.deed: pulled a stranger out of a ravine

text: The rock comes away under your hand. You fall the last ten feet, and neither of you is getting up that way.

options.label: Call down that you will send help

text: You promise to tell someone at the next village. Whether anyone comes in time is not your business, you tell yourself.

rockfall.name: a rockfall across the way
intro: The way ahead is gone under a slide of broken rock and earth, fresh enough that dust still hangs over it.
A boulder the size of a cottage has come down in the night and brought half the slope with it across the path.
Rubble, roots and a smashed tree block the way. Somewhere above, small stones are still trickling down.

options.label: Dig a way through with your shovel

text: An hour of digging and the loose earth gives way to a gap you can squeeze through.

options.label: Lever the stones aside with your crowbar

text: The bar goes under the big stones one by one, and over they go, down the slope with a roar.
A stone rolls the wrong way and over your foot. In the end you are through, and limping.
Over the top on hands and knees, with the whole pile shifting under you, and down the far side.
The pile moves. You come down the far side faster than you meant to, with stones after you.
Three hours up and down the hillside to get back to where you would have been.

old_well.name: an old well
intro: A ring of mossy stones in the grass: a well, from some farm long gone. Far down, something catches the light.
An old well-head with no bucket and no house near it. Drop a stone and you hear it hit something that is not water.
A well, dry, its stones half fallen in. At the bottom, among the leaves, there is the shape of a bundle someone threw down there.

text: Down the rope into the cold. In the leaves at the bottom: a purse gone green, and what somebody did not want found.
The rope burns your hands and you come down hard. At the bottom: leaves, bones of something small, and nothing else.

options.label: Fish for it with your grappling hook

text: Twenty casts, and the hook comes up with a rotten bundle on it: coins, and a ring.
An hour of casting into the dark brings up leaves, a bucket handle and a dead crow.
Whatever is down there has waited this long.

shut_gate._comment: Not met on the road: a walled town or city after dark, when you press > at its gate (game/state.py gate_shut).
shut_gate.name: a shut gate
intro: The gates are shut for the night. A lantern moves on the wall above, and stops.
The gate is barred. Somewhere behind it a dog barks, and a shutter in the postern slides open a hand's width.
Too late: the great doors are shut and chained, and the walls are dark but for one watch fire.

options.label: Knock at the postern and pay the warden

text: Two silver pennies through the grille, and the little door in the big one opens just wide enough.
"Late, aren't you," says the warden, and takes the coin, and lets you through the postern.
The warden hears you out, grumbles, and draws the bolt on the postern.
"Go on, then. And I never saw you." The postern opens.
"Come back at dawn like everyone else." The shutter slams.

options.label: Throw a grappling hook over the wall

text: The hook bites on the third throw, muffled in a cloak. Up the rope, over the wall where the watch is not, and down into a dark lane.
The hook rings on the stones like a bell. A lantern swings your way, and you are back in the ditch before it gets there.

options.label: Climb the wall where it is low

text: Over the wall where the stones are loose and the watch is far away, and down into a stinking alley.
Halfway up, a stone comes away in your hand. You land hard in the ditch.

options.label: Sleep under the walls until dawn

text: You find a corner out of the wind below the walls and sleep as well as you can. At dawn the gates open with a great deal of shouting.
